name: Damoclès
notes: Rock colour ranges from yellow through grey to blue.
Often physical climbing on vertical to slightly overhanging profiles.
routes: Sustained and varied. The route starts by traversing left, with lots of pinches. The exit pillar is really airy.
Slab with big holds at the start and a traverse right (crosses route 241). Then follows the line of the pillar. Very fun route.
Continuous route in an overhanging yellow corner. Athletic climbing on jugs. After the ledge, take the back of the corner.
Same start as the previous route, with a finish where you must stay on the arête of the slab.
Inconsistent climbing. The 1st part is very easy on big holds; then a bouldery section on a grey slab with small crimps needs flexibility, grip and determination.
Varied route. Slab start on edges, then a demanding corner and an easier finish. Fairly sustained overall.
A natural hive regularly occupied (bees!) on the upper slab. Magnificent route on beautiful rock. Physical, technical and slightly committing climbing in the 2nd part. A must-do.
Traversing line, as was fashionable in the '80s. Climbing on good holds broken up by ledges.
Sustained, fairly physical climbing on steep ground. A classic at the grade. Very nice, really pumpy route.
One of the most beautiful routes on the crag. An absolute must-do. It has everything: steep ground, good holds, plenty of technical moves, demanding to read — in short, a staple!
Steep climbing following a sometimes blocked crack. Demanding to read. Varied, very pleasant climbing. A must-do, one of the most beautiful at the grade.
Technical climbing on a pillar. Awkward start on a slightly overhanging pillar, then a slab with deceptive holds, easier finish. Nice route.
Inconsistent climbing. Very rough rock, cracks that need good control. Some ledges break the rhythm.
Starting variant of route 253. Slabs with good holds. Fun overall.
A great classic of the crag. Polished route that still needs care to avoid a slip. Historic route, as it was one of the first climbed free.

Sustained and varied climbing. Corner slightly polished because it is sheltered from rain; technical, complex climbing on very demanding crimps. Committing at the overhang. A benchmark route at Saffres — a good test of your level.
Finishing variant of route 257. Traverse right after the leaning slab to reach a small, slightly physical overhang. Fun route.
Overhanging slab with a saving sloper. A big dynamic move towards the top. 'Old-school' technical climbing.
Same line as route 259 lower down, then avoids the hard move on the left. Same finish. Very classy overall. A must-do.
Sustained overhanging route with a good rest. Finishes along the arête with a nice flight up jugs.
